name: vector_light_settings_gate
description: Photographs the settings page around the vector-light block, so the sub-option gate can be looked at rather than argued for. With the master switch ON the three nested controls -- pawn shadows, light through open doors, extra vibrant indoor lighting -- are live; with it OFF they are greyed and unclickable, and the two frames side by side are the whole change. THE THIRD IS NEW AND SHIPS OFF, so in the enabled arm it is live-but-unticked, which is a different state from the greyed one beside it and the distinction is the point of shooting both. THERE WERE THREE. "Lamp beam strength" was removed rather than missed by a re-shoot: the per-fragment max decides a lamp's level against vanilla's own, so the slider governed only the no-shader fallback, which no player can select or judge. The gated-looking slider still in these frames is the cloud block's "Cloud opacity", which hangs off a different master ("Visible clouds") and is therefore LIVE in both arms -- it is in shot because it shares the page, not because it is part of this gate. A THIRD ARM exists for that one and is shot the same way: "cloudSheet">False</cloudSheet> in the settings file greys the opacity slider while leaving the vector-light block alone (Tests/Screenshots/cloud_opacity_settings_gated.png). NEEDS --keep-dialogs, or the guard refuses the window at Add and the shot is a plain colony. WHICH ARM IS SHOT IS DECIDED BY THE SETTINGS FILE, not by this scenario: <vectorLights>True</vectorLights> gives the enabled arm and False the gated one, because Dialog_SettingsShot draws the real settings page and the page reads live settings. The first capture is thrown away because hideUi is only honoured from the second onwards. Waits in FRAMES, not ticks -- a forcePause modal stops the clock.
